articles.title: A joke domain purchase turned in geopolitical warfare
articles.titleZh: 一个玩笑域名的购买演变成了地缘政治战争
articles.author: kareiva

zh.thesis: 一个业余无线电探空仪追踪网站，无意间记录了军事活动，卷入间谍气球、俄乌战争，甚至接到了美国战争部的数据请求。
paragraphs: 2018 年，作者注册了 sondehub.org，最初只是个玩笑——把访问者重定向到一个追踪气象气球的网站。当时澳大利亚追踪探空仪的爱好者还很少，网站只是为了避开默认过滤，看看完整的数据。
但后来，正规的 Habhub 服务器撑不住了，他们开始自己接手数据，还开发了反向预测系统。这系统能根据已升空气球的轨迹，反推出它的发射地点。
问题在于，风数据不仅能用来预报天气，还能用于炮兵测距。他们无意中把军事发射点标上了地图，还探测到海上的军舰。军方发来邮件，希望别把敏感地点标出来，他们同意了，删除了那些点。
2023 年的「中国间谍气球」事件让网站流量激增。之后他们收到大量来自军方和政府的请求。那一年，美国用导弹击落了一个业余气球，之后他们的 API 就频繁被爬取，甚至被用于预测无人机或导弹的轨迹，推测与俄乌战争有关。
他们发现有人在使用他们的预测系统，为了安全，他们迅速提供了一个本地运行方案，而不是切断服务。他们还联系了 AWS，强调不能封锁那个账户——因为可能造成生命损失。
2025 年，美国「战争部（情报与安全）」向他们索取数据。因为数据本是公开的，他们决定至少收点钱。但发票寄出后，对方再没回复。他们还接到过 NTSB 关于气球与飞机碰撞的询问，以及 FAA 关于气象气球存在性的咨询，还有寻找捡到探空仪却撞坏房子逃逸的人。
这个故事从玩笑开始，却一步步卷入世界大事。它揭示了业余爱好者的公开数据如何被军事和情报部门使用，也展现了背后的伦理困境。作者最后说，这还不是全部，也许会有下篇。

en.thesis: A hobby balloon-tracking website accidentally mapped military launch sites and got pulled into spy balloon incidents, the Ukraine war, and a request from the U.S. Department of War.
paragraphs: In 2018, the author registered sondehub.org as a joke—a redirect to a site that tracked weather balloons. Back then, few Australians chased radiosondes, and the site just removed the default filter so hobbyists could see the full data.
But when the original Habhub servers buckled, they took over the data and built a reverse-prediction system. It could take a balloon already in flight and work backwards to find its launch site.

The problem: wind data isn''t just for weather forecasting—it''s also used for artillery ranging. They had accidentally mapped military launch sites and even spotted naval vessels at sea. The military asked them not to mark sensitive locations on maps, and they agreed, deleting those points.

The 2023 China spy balloon incident brought a surge of traffic. After that, they received many requests from military and government users. That year, after a U.S. missile shot down an amateur balloon, their API started getting scraped more and more, suspected of being used to predict drone or missile trajectories, likely connected to the Ukraine war.

When they discovered someone was using their prediction system, they quickly released a local version to run independently, rather than cutting them off. They also contacted AWS, stressing that the source account must not be blocked—loss of life could occur.

In 2025, the U.S. Office of the Secretary of War (Intelligence and Security) asked for data. Since the data was already public, they decided to at least charge for it. But the invoice was never paid. They also got queries from the NTSB about a balloon-plane collision, from the FAA asking if weather balloons even exist, and from a property owner looking for someone who hit a barn while picking up a radiosonde.

What started as a joke turned into a story about how hobbyist public data gets used by militaries and spy agencies, and the ethical dilemmas that follow. The author ends by noting this isn''t everything—there might be a part two.

articles.title: I Was Compelled to Revisit: Rory Kennedy on “Freefall: A Reckoning For Boeing”
articles.titleZh: 《自由落体：波音的清算》导演谈为何重访波音
articles.author: Nell Minow

zh.thesis: 波音自合并以来不断以利润换安全，导致危机，而法律与监管至今未真正追责。
paragraphs: 导演 Rory Kennedy 在《坠落》之后推出续作《自由落体》，因为波音没有吸取教训。737 MAX 两起空难后，公司承认是 MCAS 系统的问题，却没有人为责任入狱。
复飞后事故不断，引擎脱落、舷窗爆裂。吹哨人 John Barnett 在作证期间神秘死亡，更多人主动联系导演，展示工厂内部的真相。
影片揭露，从麦道合并、总部迁离西雅图到照搬韦尔奇的股东至上模式，波音早已抛弃质量与安全，一切为奖金和股价让路。
但牺牲长期信誉和金钱换来的短期成本削减，让公司持续亏损。导演直言，这样下去波音是自毁。
政策上，司法部的新一届政府撤回了认罪协议，FAA 预算被削减，监管形同虚设。导演呼吁选民关注官员是否支持监管，才有可能带来改变。

en.thesis: Boeing has traded safety for profit since its mergers, and the legal and regulatory systems have yet to hold anyone accountable.
paragraphs: Director Rory Kennedy follows her first film with 'Freefall' because Boeing has not learned its lesson. After the two 737 MAX crashes, the company admitted the MCAS system was at fault, but no one has gone to prison.

Since the planes returned to the sky, accidents have piled up — engines falling off, a window blowing out. Whistleblower John Barnett died under suspicious circumstances while testifying, and more insiders reached out to show what happens inside the factory.

The film traces the rot to the McDonnell Douglas merger, the move of headquarters away from Seattle, and the Jack Welch model of shareholder first. Quality and safety gave way to bonuses and stock price.
Short-term cost cutting has destroyed long-term reputation and money; the company keeps losing. The director says Boeing is self-destructing.

The previous administration had Boeing plead guilty, then the next one dropped it. The FAA is starved of funds and its oversight gutted. Kennedy urges voters to back officials who regulate corporations.

articles.title: Pluralistic: The ordinariness of evil (19 Aug 2026)
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

zh.thesis: AI 公司的所谓「毁灭性潜力」其实是营销话术，我们不该助长它，而该把 AI 当作普通技术来对待。
paragraphs: AI 老板们天天公开哀叹自家产品的可怕潜力：未来会抢走工作，甚至觉醒后把人类变成回形针。听着像在担忧，其实每句担忧都是一句吹嘘——因为 AI 现在有的只是潜力。
实际存在的 AI 只是在边缘有用：熟练的人能分辨对错输出，谨慎集成才能有点价值。多数时候它就是个新奇玩具，顶多像文字处理器的插件。
但正常技术不该换来一年一万亿美元的投资，以及各国公务员被批量裁员换成 AI。这些人押上全部身家，当然要说 AI 是万能机器，被问急了就改口说「即将」万能。
AI 确实有破坏性潜力，但不在它自己，而在我们：老板们陷入囚徒困境，谁都不肯承认花的钱打了水漂，于是越赌越大；数据中心的泡沫让官员放弃环评，强征民宅农田；它还狂耗水电、排放巨量碳。
所以要批评的是这些实实在在的破坏，而不是帮他们吹嘘。伯尼·桑德斯别再说政府该持股 50%，该说的是泡沫破裂时绝不救助；也别再谈什么「AI 安全」「失控 AI」，公司安全工具逃逸了，该问的是「你怎么连个沙盒都做不好」。
更重要的是，别把 AI 说得特别邪恶。用 AI 不会让你变坏或发疯，就像过山车只是触发你本来就有心脏病。AI 就是普通电脑，服务器破产贱卖后照样能跑开源模型，不会传染罪恶。
把 AI 说成恶魔，等于把萨姆·奥尔特曼这种平庸货色捧成超级反派，让他更轻松地融资。批评的正确姿势是指出他们在撒谎，而不是复述他们的谎言再补一句「这样不好」。

en.thesis: AI companies' talk of 'destructive potential' is marketing, and we should stop amplifying it and treat AI as an ordinary technology.
paragraphs: AI bosses are always publicly lamenting the terrible potential of their products: they will take jobs, wake up and turn us into paperclips. It sounds like worry, but every worry is a boast, because all AI has right now is potential.

Actual AI is only useful at the margins: skilled people who can tell correct output from wrong, and who integrate it carefully, get something out of it. For most it is a toy, little better than a word-processor plug-in.

But a normal technology does not warrant a trillion dollars a year in investment, or civil servants fired en masse and replaced with AI. Those who have staked everything on AI will call it the everything machine, and when pressed, admit it will be the everything machine once it starts doing AI research, which it cannot.

AI does have destructive potential, but not in itself. Bosses are trapped in a prisoner's dilemma, none willing to admit their money and jobs were wasted, so they double down; the data-center bubble has towns tossing out environmental review, seizing homes and farms; it devours water and energy and emits gigatons of carbon.

So the criticism should target these real harms, not the hype. Bernie Sanders should stop demanding the government own half of these money-losers and start saying they will get no bailout when the bubble bursts; drop the talk of 'AI safety' and 'rogue AI'. When a company's security tool escapes, ask why they are so bad at building sandboxes.

Above all, stop treating AI as exceptionally evil. Using it does not make you evil or mad, any more than a carnival ride triggers a heart attack you never knew you had. They are just computers; sold off at ten cents on the dollar, they can still run open models without infecting you with sin.

Calling AI a demon turns mediocrities like Sam Altman into super-villains and helps them raise money. The right way to criticize them is to point out they are lying, not to repeat their lies as warnings.

articles.title: Pluralistic: IP can't save you from AI (18 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: IP 救不了你免受 AI 之害
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

zh.thesis: 靠版权来对抗 AI 对劳动的侵蚀是失败策略，真正的出路在于劳动权和隐私权。
paragraphs: 作者 Cory Doctorow 认为，资本押注 AI 是因为想裁掉所有工人，艺术家也是工人，应该保护自己的劳动利益。但很多同行认为扩大版权就能解决，比如禁止抓取、分析、发布分析结果，也就是禁止训练 AI。
这是失败策略。禁止抓取和分析会误伤大量有益活动，从《牛津英语词典》到搜索引擎、互联网档案馆都依赖未经许可的大规模分析。而且根本写不出只禁止“坏”用途的法律，25 年互联网政策经验表明这几乎不可能。
更关键的是，版权给了艺术家权利，却没给谈判筹码。创意行业被垄断成五大出版商、四大制片厂、三大唱片、两大应用商店、一个电子书平台，富豪老板更富，艺术家更穷，版权延长也没用，因为工人没有议价权。
工人该靠劳动权，不是版权。编剧工会靠罢工赢了 AI，靠的是部门集体谈判，但 1947 年《塔夫脱-哈特利法》禁止了它，恢复很难。而版权是老板也想要的，所以即使赢了，钱也进老板口袋，AI 还是用来压工资。
今天有个实例：Spirit 航空破产，托管人把全部员工数据卖给 Google 训练 AI。这些邮件、备忘录、日历都是员工写的，但按“职务作品”归公司，所以成了破产资产。2001 年安然破产后邮件公开，成了“安然语料库”，被用来研究社交操控，158 名员工的隐私受害至今。
美国劳动法和隐私法都保护不了员工，隐私法最后一部还是 1988 年的《视频隐私保护法》。Google 说会“去标识化”，但这是幻想，随时可能被重新识别。版权代替不了劳动权和隐私权，就像用购物代替政治一样徒劳。
所以别再假装自己是小企业，要求更多版权只是给了老板帮凶的武器。真正该做的是联合所有工人争取部门集体谈判，联合所有消费者争取隐私权。赢回劳动权和隐私权，才有制止 AI 的权利，而不仅仅是愤怒。

en.thesis: Copyright cannot save creative workers from AI; labor and privacy rights can.
paragraphs: Cory Doctorow argues that capital is betting on AI because it wants to fire all workers. Artists are workers too, and should protect their labor interests. But many peers think expanding copyright is the answer, like banning scraping, analysis, and publishing analysis, which is what training AI means.

That is a losing strategy. Banning scraping and analysis would hurt many beneficial activities, from the OED to search engines to the Internet Archive, which rely on unlicensed mass analysis. And it is nearly impossible to write a law that only bans 'bad' uses, as 25 years of internet policy experience shows.

More crucially, copyright gives artists rights but not bargaining leverage. The creative industries are concentrated into five publishers, four studios, three labels, two app stores, one ebook platform. Bosses are richer, artists poorer, and extended copyright hasn't helped because workers lack bargaining power.

Workers should rely on labor rights, not copyright. The Writers Guild beat AI with a strike, using sectoral bargaining, but it was banned by the Taft-Hartley Act in 1947, making it hard to restore. Copyright is what bosses want too, so even winning it, the money goes to bosses, and AI still erodes wages.

Today's example: Spirit Airlines went bankrupt, and trustees sold all employee data to Google for AI training. Those emails, memos, and calendar entries were written by workers, but as 'works made for hire' they belong to the company, so they became bankruptcy assets. In 2001, Enron emails became public as the 'Enron Corpus,' used to study social manipulation, and 158 employees still suffer privacy invasions.

US labor and privacy laws offer little protection; the last privacy law was the Video Privacy Protection Act of 1988. Google promises 'de-identification,' but that's a pipe dream, vulnerable to re-identification. Copyright cannot replace labor and privacy rights, just as shopping cannot replace politics.

So stop pretending to be small businesses; demanding more copyright gives bosses a weapon to help them. The real path is to unite all workers for sectoral bargaining and all consumers for privacy rights. Winning those rights gives you the right to do something about AI, not just be angry.

articles.title: If this is true, the hyperscalers are toast
articles.titleZh: 如果这是真的，超大规模云厂商就惨了
articles.author: Joachim Klement

zh.thesis: 斯坦福的研究显示，本地小模型已能胜任八成任务，超大规模云厂商的巨额投资可能打水漂。
paragraphs: 斯坦福最近的研究对比了本地小模型和云端大模型。小模型能装在个人电脑或手机上，大模型跑在数据中心里。如果结果属实，未来可能不需要那么多数据中心了。
在聊天任务上，小模型在 98.6% 的情况下不输大模型。推理任务上也追得很快，平均 62.5% 的情况持平或更好。综合来看，81.2% 的任务小模型够用。
而且小模型能耗和算力成本低 50% 到 85%。它的每瓦推理能力是大模型的七倍。能本地解决的任务，就没必要发到云端。
不过最难的推理任务、代理型 AI 应用，小模型还差得远。手机上的模型也远不如桌面电脑上的。但优势每年都在缩小。
对投资者来说，数据中心可能是 AI 领域最差的投资。如果七成到八成的任务都能本地跑，云厂商的收入增长撑不起资本开支。真正的赢家可能是戴尔、苹果这类桌面电脑厂商。

en.thesis: Stanford's research suggests local small models can handle most tasks, putting the hyperscalers' huge investments at risk.
paragraphs: Recent Stanford research compared small language models running locally with large ones in data centers. Small ones can fit on personal computers or phones; big ones need the cloud. If the results hold, we may not need so many data centers.
On chat tasks, small models match or beat large ones 98.6% of the time. They catch up fast on reasoning too, tying or winning 62.5% on average. Overall, they suffice for 81.2% of tasks.
Small models use 50% to 85% less energy and compute. Their inference per watt is seven times higher. Anything that can run locally, should.
But on the hardest reasoning and agentic AI, they still lag. Phone models are much weaker than desktop ones. Yet the gap narrows every year.
For investors, data centers may be the worst AI bet. If 70-80% of tasks go local, cloud revenue won't justify the capex. The real winners might be Dell and Apple.

articles.title: Why I'm Staying Out Of The Substack Religion Debate
articles.titleZh: 为什么我不参与 Substack 上的宗教大辩论
articles.author: Scott Alexander

zh.thesis: 关于神的争论之所以让人提不起兴趣，是因为相信神本质上就是相信一个无法证伪的强大实体干预了历史，这跟相信外星人帮助拿破仑一样离谱。
paragraphs: 最近 Substack 上又掀起了一波宗教与无神论的大辩论，这让我想起本世纪初的博客圈。我以前挺喜欢参与这种讨论，但现在却提不起劲了。
我觉得我的无神论不是靠精细推理得来的，而是像常识一样先于这些论证而存在。好比外星人帮拿破仑打胜仗的故事，人们不会去逐条反驳，而是从一开始就觉得荒唐。
这种「强大实体干预历史」的理论其实什么问题都能解释，比真正的原因更完美。就像说数字 42 是答案，问你为什么，你说因为有个隐藏的实体想让它是这个答案。
实际上每个文明都这么干过：古人不理解闪电，就说是雷神发怒；不理解太阳，就说是太阳神在驱赶黑暗之龙。随着科学进步，这些解释一个个被抛弃了。
所以当我看到有人说「宇宙的存在、意识、微调这些未解之谜，背后肯定有个强大的意识想要这样」时，我还没听就开始翻白眼了。
神学家可能会说，神是无限简单的存在，所以不需要过度惩罚。但这是诡辩，因为「无限」其实是无限复杂，让一个无限的存在比一个有限的飞机更简单，这显然是颠倒黑白。
就算退一步，把心智视为神秘实体，但计算能力显然不需要这些。大脑受损、药物影响、基因差异，都改变计算能力，而我们对大脑的工作机制了解得越多，就越发现双元神论的余地。
因此，神学论证顶着「过度拟合」的帽子，我要么懒得参与，要么像现在这样写篇文章说明我为什么不参与。

en.thesis: The God debate leaves me cold because belief in God essentially amounts to an unfalsifiable powerful-entity explanation of history, as absurd as believing aliens helped Napoleon.
paragraphs: Substack recently saw a wave of theism-versus-atheism debates, echoing the early-2000s blogosphere. I enjoyed those back then, but now I can't muster the interest.

My atheism feels less like a product of fine-grained reasoning and more like common sense that precedes argument. Consider the claim that aliens helped Napoleon win battles: nobody bothers to refute it point by point, it's just absurd on its face.
A 'powerful entity intervened' explanation for anything is strictly superior to any real account, because it can explain any pattern whatsoever. It's the ultimate overfit.

Every culture in history has resorted to it: thunder was the Storm God, the sun was the Sun God driving away the Dragon of Darkness. As science filled in the gaps, one by one those explanations were dropped.
So when someone says the remaining anomalies — existence, consciousness, fine-tuning — are the work of an intentional, hidden, exotic intelligence, I start rolling my eyes before hearing the details.

Theologians might argue that God is a 'simple' being because He is unlimited, so the overfitting penalty doesn't apply. But that's a sleight of hand: subtracting limits from a concept is just adding complexity. An infinite mind is far more complex than a finite airplane.

And even if consciousness does have an exotic substrate, computation clearly runs on ordinary physics: brain damage, drugs, and genetics all alter it predictably, and we've built AIs from the same principles. Whatever dualism remains, it doesn't buy you infinite computing power.
So the whole edifice carries enough of an overfitting penalty that I'd rather not descend into the weeds of these debates — or at most, I'll write this post about why I'm not participating.

articles.title: An LLM wiki changed how I work
articles.titleZh: LLM 维基如何改变我的工作方式
articles.author: Casey Newton

zh.thesis: 用 LLM 自动整理个人知识库的维基，能大幅提升工作效率，但需要持续维护。
paragraphs: 四月初，AI 研究者 Andrej Karpathy 在推上分享了一个想法：用 LLM 把本地文档整理成 Markdown 维基，并自动更新。这个想法立刻在网上爆红，我也决定花几周时间试试。
结果非常有用。我先把整个 Platformer 档案喂给它，它自动提取了所有人物、公司和概念，生成了 1440 多个页面，我的 Meta 页面超过 1.2 万字，链接到 1300 多个其他页面。
每天早晨，我用 Obsidian 的剪藏工具把新闻存进维基，脚本自动归类。遇到复杂故事，比如 OpenAI 代理安全事件，我每天打开页面就能回忆细节，还能直接跳转原始来源，省了很多时间。
它还自动生成新概念页面，比如「tokenmaxxing」，并更新首页。这让我很容易发现新选题，比如最近看到「AI 与国会」页面，就促成了一个播客选题。
但维基需要频繁维护：页面太长要压缩，代码出错要修，而且 Claude 生成的风格太压缩，我不得不用 GPT-5.6 Sol 重写系统，让它更接近 AP 风格。
虽然有点笨重，但它是我今年尝试的工具里最有用的。它就像我 2008 年开始用 Evernote 以来的终极形态——一个自组织的知识库。

en.thesis: An LLM-maintained personal wiki dramatically improves productivity, but requires constant upkeep.
paragraphs: In early April, AI researcher Andrej Karpathy tweeted an idea: use an LLM to organize local documents into a Markdown wiki that updates itself. It went viral, and I decided to spend a few weeks trying it.

It worked remarkably well. I seeded it with the entire Platformer archive, and it extracted all the people, companies, and concepts, generating over 1,440 pages. My Meta page runs over 12,000 words and links to 1,300 others.

Each morning I clip news into the wiki via Obsidian, and a script organizes it. For complex stories like the OpenAI agentic breach, I pull up the page daily to refresh my memory and jump to original sources, saving hours.
It also auto-generates pages for new concepts like 'tokenmaxxing' and updates a home page. That recently helped me spot 'AI and Congress' and pitch a podcast segment.
But the wiki needs constant maintenance: pages grow too long, code breaks, and Claude's compressed style was unreadable, so I had GPT-5.6 Sol rewrite the system to AP style.
Clunky as it is, it's the most useful tool I've tried this year. It's the endgame of what started when I installed Evernote in 2008 — a self-organizing knowledge base.

articles.title: Why You Move Factors in to Whether It Protects You From Dementia
articles.titleZh: 为什么运动的护脑效果取决于你怎么动
articles.author: Jake Currie

zh.thesis: 运动能否预防痴呆，取决于运动的场景：休闲运动降低风险，重体力劳动却增加风险。
paragraphs: 长期以来，我们知道规律运动能降低痴呆风险。但《柳叶刀·公共卫生》上新的荟萃分析发现，这个关联有个前提：得看运动发生在什么场景。
研究覆盖 420 多万成年人，发现休闲运动（跑步、骑车、打球）的人痴呆风险降低 24%，而从事重体力劳动的人风险反而升高 20%。
这被称为「体力活动悖论」，以前在心血管疾病上已发现，现在扩展到了痴呆。可能原因：休闲运动减压、常带社交，而重体力劳动重复、缺恢复、暴露于噪音和污染，还会挤掉锻炼时间。
不过这是观察性研究，不能确定因果。但加上上月那篇关于久坐场景的研究——动脑的久坐比被动久坐更护脑——结论指向同一件事：保护大脑，场景和活动本身一样重要。

en.thesis: Whether exercise protects against dementia depends on the context: leisure activity lowers risk while physically demanding work raises it.
paragraphs: We have long known that regular activity is tied to a lower dementia risk. But a new meta-review in The Lancet Public Health finds a key caveat: the context of the activity matters.
The study, covering over 4.2 million adults, found that leisure-time exercise (running, cycling, sports) cut dementia risk by 24 percent, while physically demanding jobs raised it by 20 percent.

Called the 'physical activity paradox', it was already known for heart disease, and now extends to dementia. Possible reasons: leisure exercise relieves stress and often involves socializing, while tough jobs are repetitive, lack recovery, expose workers to noise and pollution, and leave little time for exercise.

This is observational, so causality is unproven. But with last month's finding that mentally engaging seated activities (like desk work) protect the brain more than passive sitting, the verdict is the same: context is as important as the movement itself.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Text Watermarking Proves AI Companies Do Not Care at All About Writing
articles.titleZh: Anthropic 的文本水印证明 AI 公司根本不在乎写作
articles.author: Jason Koebler

zh.thesis: Anthropic 的文本水印技术把用词视为可互换的随机选择，这暴露了它对写作这门手艺的轻视。
paragraphs: Anthropic 前不久宣布，未来的 Claude 生成文本时会带上水印，让人能认出这是 AI 写的。但当时没说怎么实现。最近一篇博客揭晓了方法：通过改变选词的随机性来嵌入标记，读者看不见，但持有密钥的人能检测出来。
公司解释说，像「阴天」和「灰蒙蒙」这样的同义词，多数情况下选哪个都不影响意思，所以可以悄悄调整。但任何写过东西的人都知道，这两个词并不总是能互换，选哪个可能关乎语气、意境甚至微妙的含义。
Anthropic 声称水印不影响输出质量，评测显示创意、可读性都没变。但他们的质量测评，是让用户给聊天机器人的回答点赞或点踩，准确率差 0.01%。这根本不是衡量「写作」好坏的方式。
更让人不满的是，Anthropic 把写作描述成概率游戏，用词只是「随机数生成器」的产物。但对人来说，选哪个词浓缩了个人经历、情绪和风格，这正是人类写作和 AI 文本的差别。
这次水印技术是为应对欧盟 AI 法规，但博文的口吻恰恰暴露了公司的态度：词是可有可无的，语言是随机的。它把写作当成了可替换的零件，而不是需要心血的手艺。

en.thesis: Anthropic's text watermarking treats word choice as interchangeable randomness, revealing its contempt for the craft of writing.
paragraphs: Earlier this month, Anthropic announced that future versions of Claude would watermark their text so it could be spotted as AI-generated. It did not say how. A weekend blog post revealed the method: by subtly altering how words are chosen, the text gets a pattern readable to anyone with the key, but invisible to normal readers.

The company argued that choices like 'grey' versus 'overcast' rarely change the meaning, so they are low-stakes and can be nudged. But anyone who writes knows those words are not always interchangeable; the choice can carry tone, mood, and nuance.

Anthropic claims watermarking has no impact on quality, citing tests where users gave thumbs up or down. The difference was 0.01%. But that is a terrible way to judge writing quality—it is not someone reading carefully, just pressing a button on a chatbot reply.

The blog post describes writing as a probabilistic game, where the next word is picked by a random number generator. But for a human, choosing a word draws on personal history, mood, and style—that is what makes human writing feel alive, not generic.

The move responds to upcoming EU AI regulations, but the announcement reveals a deeper attitude: words are fungible, language is random, and writing is just filler. Anthropic, which has already been criticized for training on stolen content, shows it sees writing as a disposable product, not a craft.

articles.title: What Happens If OpenAI Dies?
articles.titleZh: 如果 OpenAI 倒闭会怎样？
articles.author: Ed Zitron

zh.thesis: OpenAI 的经济状况极其危险，很可能在 2030 年前耗尽资金，其崩溃将造成系统性冲击。
paragraphs: OpenAI 正处于极端困境：巨额亏损、增长放缓、负债累累，且主要投资方已显露疲态。本文分析了它如何运筹资金、可能倒闭的几种情形，以及倒下的后果。
OpenAI 2025 年亏损 209 亿美元，收入只有 130.7 亿。它必须在未来三年半内支付超过 8000 亿美元的算力账单，这意味着每年至少要融资 1000 亿到 2000 亿美元。
融资变得越来越难。上一轮 1220 亿美元中，亚马逊、英伟达和软银占了 1100 亿，其他风投只凑了 120 亿。而软银已流动性紧张，英伟达也表示这是最后一次大规模投资。
更糟的是，OpenAI 的营收增长在放缓，而对手 Anthropic 增速更快、客户更优质，并可能在 9 月上市，给 OpenAI 带来更大压力。
如果 OpenAI 倒闭，最先受到冲击的是依赖它的合作方，如 CoreWeave 和 Cerebras，因为它们大部分收入来自 OpenAI。微软、谷歌等超大企业也会因应收款项受影响。
可能的结局包括：微软吞并 OpenAI、被允许破产、或与 Anthropic 合并。但显然没有一个好结果。OpenAI 的崩溃可能引发连锁反应，甚至威胁软银的生存。
所以，现在就必须认真讨论 OpenAI 倒闭的可能性，而不是回避。它的承诺已经大到无法兑现，而其崩溃的后果可能堪比 Enron 和雷曼兄弟。

en.thesis: OpenAI's finances are so bad that it may run out of money before 2030, and its collapse would be systemic.
paragraphs: OpenAI is in dire straits: massive losses, slowing growth, crushing obligations, and its key backers are showing strain. This article looks at how it is funding itself, how it could fall, and what happens next.
OpenAI lost $20.9 billion in 2025 on revenue of $13.07 billion. It owes over $800 billion in compute commitments over the next three and a half years, which means raising $100-200 billion every year.

Raising money is getting harder. The last $122 billion round included $110 billion from Amazon, NVIDIA and SoftBank; venture capital only supplied $12 billion. And SoftBank is short on cash, while NVIDIA has said its $30 billion investment is likely its last.
Worse, revenue growth is decelerating, while rival Anthropic is growing faster, has a stronger enterprise base, and may IPO in September, putting OpenAI under even more pressure.

If OpenAI fails, the first casualties are its counterparties: CoreWeave and Cerebras depend on OpenAI for most of their revenue. Hyperscalers like Microsoft and Google will also take a hit from unpaid bills.
Possible scenarios: Microsoft absorbs OpenAI, it goes bankrupt, or it merges with Anthropic. None is pretty. A failure could trigger a chain reaction that threatens even SoftBank.
So it is time to seriously discuss the possibility of OpenAI's collapse. Its promises are unkeepable, and the fallout could rival Enron and Lehman Brothers.

articles.title: Arabic has four words for sadness. Philosophy explains why
articles.titleZh: 阿拉伯语有四个表示悲伤的词，哲学解释了原因
articles.author: Chereen Shurafa

zh.thesis: 阿拉伯语有多个表示悲伤的词，这反映了人类情感并非单一的，而是需要细腻区分。
paragraphs: 我们普遍认为悲伤是一种基本情绪，但阿拉伯语中却有四个词来描述它的不同面向。
哲学认为，语言并非被动地反映现实，而是主动塑造我们感知和表达情感的方式。
因此，丰富的词汇不仅仅是语言特色，它拓宽了我们理解自身内心世界的可能性。

en.thesis: Arabic's multiple words for sadness reflect the idea that human emotions are not monolithic but require fine-grained distinction.
paragraphs: We often think of sadness as a single basic emotion, yet Arabic has four words for it.
Philosophy suggests that language doesn't just mirror reality but shapes how we perceive and express emotions.
So the rich vocabulary is not a mere linguistic curiosity; it expands how deeply we can understand our inner lives.

articles.title: The Generalizability Problem, the Natural Field Experiments Answer
articles.titleZh: 可推广性问题，自然现场实验的答案
articles.author: conversableeconomist

zh.thesis: 小规模研究的结论往往推广不到大范围，原因是人在真实生活里和在被观察时表现不同，所以研究者应该设计参与者浑然不知的实验。
paragraphs: 社会科学有个老问题：小规模研究的结果能不能推广到更大范围？某个学区有效的项目，换到别的学区、全州、全国甚至其他国家，还会有效吗？这问题没有简单答案。
经济学家 John List 举例：美国的 Scared Straight 项目让高危青少年去监狱跟重刑犯面对面，试点时效果很好，80-90% 的参与者没惹麻烦，但推广后不仅没用，有些地方的犯罪行为反而上升了。
关键在于人和人不一样，所处的社会、经济、文化也不同。而且参与者一旦知道自己被研究，注意力本身就是一种干扰。List 主张做「自然现场实验」：让参与者不知道自己参与了研究。
比如审计研究：派不同族裔但对情况类似的助理去租房、贷款、买车或求职，看对方反应是否不同。List 是沃尔玛的首席经济学家，团队正对 6000 多家供应商做实验，测试怎样激励他们减排最有效。

en.thesis: Findings from small studies often fail to scale, because people behave differently when they know they are being watched, so researchers should design experiments participants never notice.
paragraphs: Social science has an old problem: do the findings of a small study carry over to a larger scale? A program that works in one school district — will it work in another, statewide, nationally, in other countries? There is no simple answer.

Economist John List gives the example of Scared Straight, which brought at-risk teenagers face to face with maximum-security inmates. In the pilot it worked well, with 80–90 percent staying out of trouble, but scaled up it failed — in some places teen crime even rose.

The key is that people differ, in their societies, economies and cultures. And once participants know they are in a study, the attention itself is a distortion. List argues for 'natural field experiments', where participants never know they are being studied.

A classic form is the audit study: send out assistants with similar credentials but different races to rent an apartment, get a loan or apply for a job, and watch for different treatment. List is chief economist at Walmart, where his team is running such experiments with over 6,000 suppliers, testing what most effectively nudges them to cut carbon emissions.

articles.title: ‘There are 1.5 sex scenes, and the food looks just fine’
articles.titleZh: 《有 1.5 场性爱场面，食物看起来还不错》
articles.author: Vittles

zh.thesis: 这部关于安东尼·波登的传记片安全但乏味，只拍了一个普通少年的夏天，完全回避了他成人人格中那些生动的部分。
paragraphs: 影评人艾米莉·威尔逊曾嘲讽《奥德赛》改编电影里的食物糟糕，而《托尼》这部电影里食物看起来还不错，性爱场面有 1.5 场——这是它仅有的优点。
影片改编自波登的回忆录《厨房机密》，只选取了开头的章节：1975 年夏天，少年托尼在普罗文斯敦的餐厅洗碗，整天想着追女孩。
原著里的波登是个自封的感官主义者，对生蚝和食物充满欲望，而电影里的托尼只是个令人讨厌的中产小孩，这段经历普普通通，没有任何鲜明的特点。
传记片要种下人物成年后的人格种子，但这部电影刻意避开了波登的好奇心、性感和与人相处的天赋，既不打算也不愿意触碰他人生中的广度、戏剧性和复杂性。
所以这不是波登的故事，只是一个名字恰好叫托尼的少年的夏天。想要在银幕上看到那个作为文化探险家的波登，还是去重温《未知之旅》吧。

en.thesis: This biopic of Anthony Bourdain is safe but bland, showing an ordinary teenage summer and dodging the vivid parts of his adult persona.
paragraphs: Emily Wilson famously quipped about the food in the Odyssey film; in 'Tony' the food looks fine and there are 1.5 sex scenes, which may be its only virtues.
Adapted from Bourdain's memoir 'Kitchen Confidential', it takes only the early chapters: in the summer of 1975, teenage Tony washes dishes in Provincetown and dreams of winning over a girl.
In the book Bourdain was a self-declared sensualist, lusting after oysters and food; on screen Tony is just an obnoxious middle-class kid whose summer could be anyone's.

A biopic needs to plant the seeds of the adult persona, but this film deliberately withholds Bourdain's curiosity, his sexuality, and his way with people, and it neither wants nor tries to cover the breadth, drama, and complexity of his life.
So this is not Bourdain's story, just a boy named Tony's summer. If you want the cultural explorer on screen, rewatch 'Parts Unknown'.

articles.title: The Wonders of the Male Human Pelvis
articles.titleZh: 男性人类骨盆的奇妙之处
articles.author: Jake Currie

zh.thesis: 男性骨盆独特的髋臼朝向是一个演化适应，让男性步行更省力、更适合长距离行走。
paragraphs: 关于女性骨盆的研究很多，因为「产科困境」——人类分娩比其他哺乳动物更困难——牵扯到演化权衡、直立行走、颅骨大小等问题。男性骨盆却长期被忽视，直到现在。
《科学报告》上的一项新研究分析了 91 个现代人骨盆和两个尼安德特人男性骨盆，发现现代男性骨盆的髋臼更朝前，这是一个独特的适应特征，有利于行走。
行走可以看作一系列受控的摔倒：重心不稳，然后伸腿接住自己。每次下坠都会给关节压力，也需要能量恢复。男性骨盆让腿略微前移，股四头肌能同时吸收冲击并弹回身体，步态更高效。
研究者说，女性骨盆因分娩需求无法发展出这些改变。这些发现还有实际应用：理解行走机制的演化，有助于生物力学、康复和损伤预防的研究。

en.thesis: The male pelvis's uniquely forward-facing hip sockets are an adaptation that makes male walking more efficient and better for long distances.
paragraphs: There is a lot of research on the female pelvis, and for good reason. The 'obstetrical dilemma' — why childbirth is so hard for humans — involves evolutionary trade-offs, upright gait, skull size, and the female pelvis. The male pelvis has been neglected, until now.

A new study in Scientific Reports analyzed 91 modern human pelvises and two Neanderthal male pelvises, and found the modern male pelvis has hip sockets oriented more toward the front, a unique adaptation that benefits locomotion.

Walking is a series of controlled falls: you destabilize your center of gravity, then swing a leg to catch yourself. Each drop stresses joints and needs energy to recover. The male pelvis positions the legs slightly more forward, so the quads both absorb shock and spring the body up, making the gait more efficient.

Female pelvises couldn't develop these changes because of childbirth demands. The findings also apply beyond evolution: understanding walking mechanics can help biomechanics, rehabilitation, and injury prevention research.
